##


You Set the Rules Once, Your Agent Does the Rest


During the festival rush, flight prices go through the roof. The only way to get a good deal is to catch the fare in the exact minute it dips. But who can actually do that? You’d have to sit and watch the app all day and all night.


Diya, Yatra’s AI agent, just did it for someone. It caught a Bengaluru to Delhi fare the second it dropped to ₹11,500, at 2:47 in the morning, and paid for it with a real card. The person was fast asleep. No code to type, no approval to tap, and the agent never even saw the card number.


That’s what we launched at GFF 2026: Agentic Commerce on Cards that runs on its own. With Yatra, powered by Mastercard. AI agents could already search, compare, and pick the best option. Now they can pay too, all by themselves, inside the limits you set once.


Here’s how it works, and why you can trust it.


##


**What actually happened**


Let’s stay with that flight for a second, because nothing about it was a trick.


Earlier, the customer had given Diya one simple instruction: “Book a flight from Bengaluru to Delhi if the fare drops under ₹12,000.” Then they got on with their life. 5 days later the price finally dipped, at an hour no one would be awake for. Diya checked the rule, saw the price was right, and booked the seat on the card the customer had chosen.


That’s the whole idea. The agent isn’t off making its own decisions with your money. It only ever does what you asked it to, and only when your condition is met.


##


**You approve once, not every time**


Normally, you approve a card payment every single time you buy something. That’s the step that always needed you to be there.


Autonomous payments flip that around. You setup a pre-authorization on your card, once, by authenticating via passkey. At that moment you set your budget and your rules, and the amount is blocked and set aside for that purchase, so the money is accounted for before anything happens. After that, the agent can go ahead on its own, within those limits, without asking you again at the time of booking. That’s what let the 2:47 AM booking happen without anyone awake.


So you don’t give up control by walking away. You set the rules early, and they hold.


##


**Built on rails you already trust**


Letting an agent spend your money is a big ask, so this was built on the networks people already trust.


Every one of these payments runs on Mastercard’s network, with the same security and protections your card already carries today. Your real card number is never handed to the AI agent or the app it lives in, so there’s nothing sensitive for it to lose or misuse. The permission you give is tied to that one agent and the rules you set, and it only ever works within those limits. And because it runs on card rails, the usual things you count on, like the ability to dispute a charge, still work the way you expect.


##


**You’re always in charge**


The agent can only do what you allowed. It books the trip you asked for, stays under the price you set, and pays with the card you picked. It won’t act until your condition is met, and it can never spend more than your limit. A rupee over, and nothing happens.


##


**Where this helps first**


Some things are only possible once an agent can pay on its own:


**Waiting for the right price.** An agent can watch a fare, a sale, or a restock and buy the moment it fits the budget you gave it. No person clicking through a checkout can move that fast, which is why travel is the natural place to start. It’s exactly what Diya does on Yatra.


**Grabbing something off a wishlist.** An agent can hold an item and buy it the second the price or the stock lines up with what you wanted.


##


**Where Cashfree comes in**


We’re the layer that lets an AI agent pay securely on a customer’s behalf, and lets a business accept that payment when the agent is the one bringing the customer to checkout, all on Mastercard’s network.


We carry the trust the whole way through: keeping the real card details protected, checking every payment against the rules the customer set before any money moves, and seeing the transaction through to the business getting paid.
